# PROCESS — iteration cand_0005 (parent: cand_0003, val 1.000) — final iteration of the run

Parent is **cand_0003** (val 1.000, 40/40). cand_0004 was REJECTED (val 0.950, Δ −0.050,
`broke={50768, 59595}`) and its whole batch was reverted.

## The measurement situation, stated first because it governs every decision below

Parent val is **1.000 — 40 of 40 tasks at reward 1.0, n=1, stderr 0.0, zero flaky, zero
failing.** I re-derived this from the 40 traces rather than trusting the summary: every
`score.reward == 1.0` and every `raw.test_case_results == test_case_results_no_recalc == [1]`,
so no task is passing only via the recalc-tolerant metric. The primary metric
(`hard_no_recalc`) is 1.0 on all 40.

Two consequences I did not try to argue my way around:

1. **No edit can be ACCEPTED this iteration.** The gate accepts only a per-task improvement
   that clears a noise margin; the parent is at the ceiling, so the best attainable Δ is 0 and
   the expected outcome is "rejected on a tie, champion unchanged". That is not a reason to
   ship nothing, but it *is* a reason to refuse every speculative edit: an edit cannot buy a
   point here, it can only lose one.
2. **The REAL test bites hard.** With no failing task, almost nothing passes "targets a cluster
   that is FAILING in THIS iteration's trajectories". I found exactly **one** cluster that
   does — a crash, in code I own, that fires on 7 of the 40 traces — and shipped exactly that.

## Environment faults

**None.** All 40 traces run to completion: `rollout.error is None` everywhere, no permission
denial, no missing binary, no timeout, no gateway error, no container failure. The 7
tracebacks in the split are all raised by *my own prompt text*, not by the environment — see
below. Nothing to hand back.

## Ranked cluster list

| # | cluster | class | failing tasks | leverage | shipped? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | The step-3 verification snippet in `task_template.md` **cannot run** when `answer_position` is a single cell. `graded[RNG]` returns a bare `Cell`, so the shipped line `cells = [c.coordinate for row in graded[RNG] for c in row]` raises `TypeError: 'Cell' object is not iterable`. Deterministic, 100% of single-cell tasks. | KNOWLEDGE / broken worked example (the prompt ships code that cannot execute) | 7 of 40 (17.5%): `31628` `46897` `51-12` `55979` `56563` `8942` `9726` | 0 val points today (all 7 recovered) — recovers one wasted round + ~8–10k tokens on 17.5% of tasks, and restores the verify round as a *first-try* safety net instead of a crash the agent must repair under round pressure | **yes — E1, the only edit** |
| 2 | Same line also breaks on a **comma-separated multi-part** `answer_position` (`graded["A1:B2,D1:D5"]` raises). `prompt.md` documents that this shape exists. | KNOWLEDGE | **0 of 40** — no val task has a multi-part range | fails the REAL test: hypothetical here | no — see "deliberately skipped" |
| 3 | The eight `agree? False` overrides (census in INSIGHTS.md) | SEMANTIC | 0 — all eight are currently **correct** | any rule can only flip a right answer wrong | no — needs a failing example first |
| 4 | "A column header beats the instruction's prose" (`59196`) | SEMANTIC, UNBOUNDED | 0 | unshipped for the 4th iteration running, same reason | no |

## The one edit

### E1 — `task_template.md`, step 3 snippet: guard the range enumeration for a single cell

Lever (from `guidance/system-prompt/SKILL.md`): **#5, fix the worked example** — the example
is the format-pinning artifact the reader copies verbatim, and this one was wrong. Not a new
rule, not more prose: the same 2 lines, made executable, with the *reason* stated at the point
of use (lever #2, a rule carries further when it carries its rationale).

```diff
-cells = [c.coordinate for row in graded[RNG] for c in row]
+# openpyxl hands back a bare Cell when RNG names exactly ONE cell ("B7", "C14") and a tuple
+# of row tuples for anything larger, so the plain `for row in graded[RNG] for c in row`
+# idiom raises `TypeError: 'Cell' object is not iterable` on a single-cell answer_position.
+# Use this guarded form wherever you enumerate a range, step 1 included.
+rng_obj = graded[RNG]
+cells = ([rng_obj.coordinate] if hasattr(rng_obj, "coordinate")
+         else [c.coordinate for row in rng_obj for c in row])
```

**Which file and why `task_template.md`, not `prompt.md`:** the defect is not a missing fact,
it is a defective copyable artifact. The agent does not reason its way to the crash — it
pastes the line. The fix has to be *in the line*. (cand_0004 put a prose warning in
`prompt.md` as well; I did not, see below.)

**VERIFY-THE-FIX.** Evidence, verbatim from this iteration's traces — `31628` round 3:

```
---> 32 cells = [c.coordinate for row in graded[RNG] for c in row]
TypeError: 'Cell' object is not iterable
```

identical final frame in `46897`, `51-12`, `55979`, `56563`, `8942`, `9726`. The correlation
with the cause is exact, not partial: the crashing set is **precisely** the set of
single-cell graded ranges in the split (`B1`, `I3`, `B6`, `'Calc'!B7`, `C14`,
`'Overview'!B5`, `J2`) — 7 single-cell tasks, 7 crashes, no crash on any of the other 33.

What the agent would have done differently: nothing but *not crash*. The strongest form of
verification available here is that the agent itself converged on this exact guard and the
round then completed — `31628`'s own repair round reads

```python
rng_obj = graded[RNG]
if hasattr(rng_obj, "coordinate"):  # single cell
    cells = [rng_obj.coordinate]
else:
    cells = [c.coordinate for row in rng_obj for c in row]
```

and `51-12` and `56563` independently wrote `cells = [graded[RNG].coordinate]`. So the
replacement idiom is not my guess about openpyxl's API — it is **observed executing
successfully against the real environment's openpyxl in three traces of this very split**,
each of which then scored 1.0. (I could not run openpyxl locally — not installed in the
optimizer sandbox — which is exactly why I chose the trace-verified guard over cand_0004's
unobserved `range_boundaries` helper.)

Cost today, measured: the 7 crashing tasks run **11 or 13 trace messages against the
uniform 9** for the other 33, i.e. one extra round each. Two of them (`46897`, `9726`)
crashed in their **step-1 inspect** round — they had copied the broken idiom out of the
step-3 snippet before ever reaching step 3 — and lost the whole inspection round, restarting
it from scratch. Fixing the snippet fixes that propagation at its source, which is why one
edit site is enough and why the comment says "step 1 included".

**Blast radius: BOUNDED.** The guard's `else` branch is the old expression, byte for byte.
For every range larger than one cell `hasattr(rng_obj, "coordinate")` is False (the object is
a `tuple`), so `cells` is the **identical list in the identical reading order** — which also
means `shown`, `left`, the non-empty count and `clashes` are all unchanged downstream. So the
33 multi-cell tasks are *provably* unaffected, not merely probably:
`51-12` `267-18` `80-42` `142-12` `227-40` `382-10` `395-36` `402-43` `416-15` `463-17`
`560-12` `38462` `39046` `45635` `47798` `48588` `48620` `48921` `50768` `54144` `2768`
`6698` `7902` `9569` `12864` `37378` `37456` `43436` `48527` `53383` `53647` `55049` `59196`
`59595`. On the 7 single-cell tasks the step-2 computation is untouched; only the
already-correct answer's *verification* stops crashing.

**Specifically w.r.t. the two tasks cand_0004 broke:** `50768` (`F12:H14`, 9 cells) and
`59595` (`C4:C19`, 16 cells) are both multi-cell. I read both traces: each copies the
`cells = [c.coordinate for row in graded[RNG] for c in row]` line verbatim and it executes
fine. Under E1 both take the `else` branch and get the same list. **E1 cannot be what broke
them** — so re-shipping it is not re-shipping a refuted edit, it is the one piece of
cand_0004 the measurement exonerates.

**Generalization:** the edit names no task, id, value, sheet, range or answer. It encodes one
openpyxl API fact that holds for every workbook.

## What I kept from cand_0004 and what I dropped (per the "rejected parent" rule)

cand_0004 bundled **six** edits and was reverted wholesale. Only one of them addressed
cluster 1; the other five were robustness speculation on shapes the split does not fail on.
Keeping only the exonerated one, and redesigning even that:

| cand_0004 edit | kept? | why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| step-3 snippet: single-cell enumeration | **kept, redesigned** | provably inert on `50768`/`59595` (both multi-cell). Redesigned: cand_0004 replaced the line with a 12-line `coords()` helper plus a new `from openpyxl.utils import range_boundaries, get_column_letter` import, an idiom **never observed running** in any trace. I used the 3-line guard the agents themselves ran successfully. Smaller diff, no new import, trace-verified. |
| step-1 "**cap this printout**, print `vals[:8] + vals[-4:]` per column" | **DROPPED — prime suspect for the regression** | this is a cap on *inspection*, the round the agent uses to see its data. `59595` has 16 graded cells and `50768` 9; a 12-of-16 truncation hides middle rows of exactly the columns the rule is derived from. It is the only cand_0004 edit that removes information the agent previously had, and both broken tasks are small-range tasks whose whole answer lives in the rows a cap would elide. Do not re-try. |
| "rounds that do not change `output_path` are the **scarce resource** … you get **three**" + deletion of "So verifying costs you nothing but a round." | **DROPPED — second suspect** | it replaces an unconditional "verify every time, it is free" with a budget the agent must ration. Discouraging the verify/fix loop is the single most expensive thing this prompt can do (iteration 1's +0.575 came from installing that loop). Never trade it for token economy. |
| step-2 `mine` key-shape paragraph | dropped | no trace shows a malformed `mine` key. Not REAL. |
| `prompt.md` sheet-prefix quote-stripping rewrite | dropped | it **rewrote** standing text that 40/40 tasks pass under, including `53383`'s malformed `worksheet2'!C3:C6`, which already works. UNBOUNDED rewrite for 0 failing tasks. |
| `prompt.md` single-cell prose warning | dropped | redundant once the snippet itself is correct. Lever-wise it is the weaker form of the same fix: the agent copies code, not warnings. Also keeps `prompt.md` **byte-identical** to the champion, halving the blast radius of this candidate. |

## Deliberately skipped, and why

- **Cluster 2 (multi-part comma ranges).** Real as an API fact, but **zero** val tasks have
  one, so it fails the REAL test. I refused it on purpose even though it is a 1-line change
  to the same snippet I was already editing — "I am in here anyway" is how a speculative edit
  gets in. Logged in INSIGHTS.md as a latent class with the fix written out, for a run whose
  split actually contains one.
- **Clusters 3 and 4 (semantic).** Every member currently scores 1.0. Editing them can only
  flip a correct answer. `9726` in particular hangs on one graded cell with no corroborating
  signal; `59196` is one pre-filled cell from flipping. Fourth iteration these are left alone,
  same measured reason.
- **Breadth generally.** The brief asks for many fixes. This split offers **one** that passes
  the three tests. I would rather hand back one verified edit than five that re-run
  cand_0004's experiment with a different wrapper — the run has now paid −0.025 (cand_0002)
  and −0.050 (cand_0004) for bundled speculation, and 0.000 for the two candidates that
  shipped only what the traces proved.

## Subagents / parallelism

None. The whole diagnosis is one deterministic pass over 40 JSON traces (crash-frame
extraction, round counting, range-shape correlation), done directly — fanning out would have
added coordination cost and no coverage. Where parallelism *would* pay on this benchmark is
noted in META_INSIGHTS.md.

## What to preserve

`prompt.md` is **unchanged, byte for byte**. In `task_template.md` the four-step
inspect → compute → verify → fix structure, the uncapped step-1 inspection, the "verifying
costs you nothing but a round" line, and all seven `{placeholders}` (verified present after
the edit) are untouched. The entire diff of this candidate is one hunk of 2 lines → 7 lines
inside one code block.
